items.title: GitHub repository hosting and GitHub–Jira linkage
items.gap: No repository/PR/issue lifecycle adapter or verified GitHub–Jira linkage workflow.
items.acceptance: Provide a scoped adapter for repository/PR evidence and an optional explicit Jira linkage; demonstrate it against an authorized project.

items.title: Jira agile planning and bug tracking
items.gap: No Jira integration procedure, issue field mapping, sprint handling or bug triage workflow.
items.acceptance: Discover available Jira connector, map requirement/acceptance/bug IDs and preserve project fields; demonstrate one authorized workflow with observable resulting issue state.

items.title: GitHub Actions CI and CD
items.gap: No GitHub Actions workflow template, permissions/events matrix or hosted run/artifact verification adapter.
items.acceptance: Prepare a project-matched workflow with explicit triggers/permissions/build/test/static analysis/artifacts, and validate the hosted run when authorized.

items.title: Docker container packaging (optional in source)
items.gap: Container build, runtime user, dependency layers and image provenance are not operationalized.
items.acceptance: Add optional project-driven container recipe with reproducible build, bounded runtime configuration and smoke evidence; avoid requiring Docker for projects that do not need it.

items.title: GoogleTest / gtest
items.gap: Generic command execution does not establish framework-specific test discovery, fixtures, assertions or reports.
items.acceptance: Inspect installed framework/version; provide a minimal meaningful example and exact collection/execution command, with observed test count and failing/passing evidence when used.

items.title: JUnit
items.gap: Generic command execution does not establish framework-specific test discovery, fixtures, assertions or reports.
items.acceptance: Inspect installed framework/version; provide a minimal meaningful example and exact collection/execution command, with observed test count and failing/passing evidence when used.

items.title: pytest
items.gap: Generic command execution does not establish framework-specific test discovery, fixtures, assertions or reports.
items.acceptance: Inspect installed framework/version; provide a minimal meaningful example and exact collection/execution command, with observed test count and failing/passing evidence when used.

items.title: SonarCloud static analysis
items.gap: No SonarCloud project/CI configuration, scope, token permissions or finding-validation adapter.
items.acceptance: Support optional SonarCloud configuration and inspect actual analysis/gate output; keep scanner success distinct from correctness.

items.title: Waterfall, V-model, iterative/incremental and risk-driven spiral selection
items.gap: No operational V-model requirement/design-to-test mapping; spiral risk-loop entry/exit/reassessment is not specified.
items.acceptance: Provide a decision rubric and a worked project mapping that pairs lifecycle artifacts with tests; use spiral loops only when explicit risks justify them.

items.title: Product lifecycle from research through support and retirement
items.gap: Usability research, sales/support/training/porting and product lifecycle coordination from diagrams are not a cohesive product lifecycle method.
items.acceptance: Offer an optional product lifecycle map with customer validation, support ownership, handoffs and retirement triggers appropriate to the project.

items.title: Project management lifecycle, planning, control and closure
items.gap: No project budget/calendar/status control or closure/lessons-learned procedure; dependency readiness is not a PMLC.
items.acceptance: Create an optional project plan linking scope, tasks, resources, schedule, risks, monitoring and closure evidence.

items.title: Security integrated throughout the SDLC
items.gap: No integrated phase checklist with security requirement IDs, security review owners and release evidence gates.
items.acceptance: Provide a proportionate secure lifecycle plan linking each consequential risk/control to phase, owner and verification evidence.

items.title: Security and privacy baseline training
items.gap: No role-based baseline/specialist learning plan or assessment.
items.acceptance: Provide optional role/asset-driven training objectives, exercises and evidence of understanding; do not assert a course was completed.

items.title: Approved toolchain and prohibited API policy
items.gap: No approved-tool compiler/linker options list, prohibited API inventory or enforcement workflow.
items.acceptance: Generate project/version-specific safe-tool options and prohibited API rules, enforce them with an appropriate checked tool and record exceptions/ownership.

items.title: Final security review and incident servicing plan
items.gap: No FSR inventory of threats/tool outputs/bug bars; emergency authority, inherited/third-party servicing and 24-hour contact coverage are unspecified.
items.acceptance: Offer a security release review and servicing plan with scope, unresolved issues, escalation contacts/authority, dependency update ownership and evidence-based release decision.

items.title: Scrum roles, artifacts, sprint goal and completion discipline
items.gap: No actionable product owner/Scrum master/developer responsibilities, product/sprint backlog ownership, sprint goal or definition-of-done guidance.
items.acceptance: Provide a lightweight role/artifact/event map with sprint goal, backlog refinement and explicit done/acceptance distinctions, tailored to an existing team.

items.title: Sprint planning and backlog breakdown
items.gap: No capacity-based sprint selection, sprint commitment/goal or product-to-sprint backlog workflow.
items.acceptance: Given prioritized backlog and capacity, prepare a sprint goal and feasible selected stories/tasks with dependencies and acceptance.

items.title: Daily standup: progress, next work and blockers
items.gap: State tracking is not a standup facilitation method; no short update/impediment resolution convention.
items.acceptance: Produce a concise evidence-grounded progress/next/blockers update and assign follow-up for impediments without claiming a meeting occurred.

items.title: Sprint review and demonstration
items.gap: No stakeholder demo/review method that captures resulting product backlog feedback.
items.acceptance: Prepare a working increment demo tied to acceptance; capture actual feedback and backlog changes when available.

items.title: Sprint retrospective and owned improvement experiment
items.gap: Missing method for what went well/poorly, choosing an improvement and checking its outcome next iteration.
items.acceptance: Facilitate a short evidence-based retrospective yielding one owned measurable process improvement and revisit date.

items.title: Visual backlog/task board flow
items.gap: No board WIP/capacity/workflow mapping or connector-backed state update method.
items.acceptance: Map project states to an optional board, preserve blocked/deferred work and update only authorized issue/task state.

items.title: INVEST user stories and acceptance criteria
items.gap: No six-part INVEST review workflow or sample story splitting; structural validation cannot determine independent/valuable/estimable/small.
items.acceptance: Review a story against each INVEST property, split where needed and produce observable acceptance examples without making INVEST mandatory for trivial changes.

items.title: XP planning game: release and iteration planning
items.gap: No two-horizon release/iteration planning with customer priorities, team capacity, estimates and risks.
items.acceptance: Given an ordered backlog, separate a tentative release plan from an iteration commitment and update both with actual learning.

items.title: Test-driven development red/green/refactor
items.gap: No explicit red→minimal green→refactor TDD workflow or worked new-behavior example. Regression-first guidance covers only part of TDD.
items.acceptance: Add optional TDD protocol demonstrating a meaningful failing test, minimal implementation and behavior-preserving refactor with observed evidence.

items.title: Pair programming pilot/navigator and rotation
items.gap: No pairing-session roles, rotation or learning/knowledge-sharing protocol.
items.acceptance: Offer optional driver/navigator collaboration with role switch and shared review checkpoints; do not confuse an AI review with human pair programming.

items.title: Collective code ownership
items.gap: No shared team ownership, bus-factor or cross-area contribution method.
items.acceptance: Define shared contribution boundaries, knowledge transfer and review expectations appropriate to the team.

items.title: Onsite customer / domain proxy collaboration
items.gap: No domain representative/proxy decision rights or availability/feedback arrangement.
items.acceptance: Identify the real domain decision-maker/proxy, decisions they own and how unresolved acceptance questions reach them.

items.title: Sustainable pace and slack
items.gap: No buffer for uncertainty, overload detection or deliberate learning/debt allocation.
items.acceptance: Offer a capacity plan with explicit slack and reprioritization triggers; do not use individual output quotas.

items.title: Lean waste, learning, late decisions, fast delivery, empowerment, integrity and whole-system optimization
items.gap: No explicit value-stream/waste analysis, last-responsible-moment decision rule or whole-flow improvement experiment.
items.acceptance: Provide an optional Lean diagnostic mapping actual delays/waste to one measured end-to-end improvement, avoiding local productivity proxies.

items.title: Individual and set-level requirement quality
items.gap: No operational semantic review of completeness, consistency, necessity, prioritization, conflicts or ambiguity across a requirement set.
items.acceptance: Supply a review checklist and worked rewrite that distinguishes syntactic validity from semantic quality and records unresolved stakeholder conflicts.

items.title: Feasibility study and alternative evaluation
items.gap: No coherent technical/economic/operational/schedule feasibility report or build/buy alternative recommendation.
items.acceptance: Produce a proportionate feasibility assessment with options, constraints, cost/effort assumptions, risks and a go/no-go rationale.

items.title: Stakeholder identification, elicitation and requirements analysis
items.gap: No technique selection procedure for facilitated meetings, role play, business-process/workflow analysis, questionnaires, checklists or document analysis.
items.acceptance: Select elicitation techniques by stakeholder/system context and preserve observations, conflicts, assumptions and source-to-requirement links.

items.title: Ethnography, situated observation and implicit work practices
items.gap: No field-observation protocol for social/organizational context, tacit work, consent, observation notes or evidence synthesis.
items.acceptance: Provide an optional scoped observation plan and separate observed workarounds/social constraints from interpretation and resulting requirements.

items.title: Functional, NFR, organizational/external/domain and user/system requirements
items.gap: No explicit taxonomy/workflow for organizational/external/domain constraints or user-to-system requirement derivation.
items.acceptance: Classify a small real requirement set, derive testable system behavior from user goals, and identify domain constraints needing current expert/primary evidence.

items.title: Security risk assessment, likelihood/impact and risk ranking
items.gap: No linked asset→threat→likelihood/impact→priority→risk-treatment register or security objective trace.
items.acceptance: Provide a small evidence/assumption-labelled risk register; include insider threats and never equate trusted doctors or access control with negligible residual risk.

items.title: SMART security objectives and risk-derived requirements
items.gap: No SMART review or risk→objective→security requirement ID linkage; the source’s example crypto/TLS settings need current task-specific verification.
items.acceptance: Derive testable security objectives with scope, measure, owner/milestone and linked risk/control/acceptance; do not infer controls eliminate insider or external risk.

items.title: Software requirements specification structure and external interfaces
items.gap: No optional SRS template or review covering product context, interfaces, assumptions/dependencies, functions, NFRs and design constraints.
items.acceptance: Provide a scalable SRS template for tasks that warrant it, with stable IDs, version/baseline and interfaces; label IEEE 830-1998 as historical rather than current authority.

items.title: Requirement review, verification and customer validation
items.gap: No systematic review of completeness/consistency/comprehensibility/modifiability/traceability or model validation.
items.acceptance: Use a semantic review protocol with stakeholder validation evidence, explicit unknowns and model-to-requirement consistency checks.

items.title: Fishbone analysis for requirements/model validation
items.gap: Fishbone is only a named diagram technique; it is not operationalized and is not itself evidence of model completeness.
items.acceptance: Provide optional cause-category/hypothesis/evidence steps and tie findings to requirement/model review without claiming causal proof from a diagram.

items.title: Forward/backward requirements traceability across architecture, design, implementation and test levels
items.gap: No complete SDLC RTM columns/IDs for architecture section, design section, files, unit/functional/system/acceptance tests; no reverse orphan detection across those artifacts.
items.acceptance: Extend an optional trace schema/validator for these artifact types with forward/backward traversal, unknown/dangling/orphan links and impact queries; do not claim semantic coverage from link existence.

items.title: Requirement baselines, impact analysis and controlled changes
items.gap: No requirement change request identity, rationale/alternatives, stakeholder impact, baseline version and accepted/rejected/deferred status workflow.
items.acceptance: Implement optional change-record schema and impact traversal through RTM, preserving decision history and required project approval rules without inventing routine gates.

items.title: Use-case diagrams: actors, system boundary, functions and associations
items.gap: Missing actor/system-boundary/use-case/association walkthrough and semantic checks.
items.acceptance: Supply an optional diagram method with actor goals, system boundary and valid relationships, plus a worked example and review checklist.

items.title: Use-case specifications with trigger, preconditions, main, alternate and exception flows
items.gap: No structured use-case template or numbered branch/rejoin/exception method linked to actor goals and acceptance tests.
items.acceptance: Provide a goal/actor/trigger/precondition/postcondition/main-flow template with step-referenced alternatives/exceptions and requirement/test links.

items.title: Evidence-grounded personas and user scenarios
items.gap: No persona/scenario creation method separating research-backed archetype from assumed fiction, goals, context and narrative.
items.acceptance: Provide optional persona/scenario template with evidence/assumptions, goal/context/actions and resulting requirements.

items.title: Test case specification, priority, preconditions, data, steps and observed results
items.gap: No explicit module/tester/priority/preconditions/data/environment/manual-step/expected-vs-actual-result fields or full-format review.
items.acceptance: Offer an extended optional case template with those fields while preserving concise automated cases; validate structural completeness and distinguish planned from actually run.

items.title: Test plan scope, quality goals, methodology, responsibilities and deliverables
items.gap: No comprehensive optional test plan with in/out scope, roles, deliverables, suspension/resumption, bug triage and completeness criteria; an external example link is not a bundled Sui plan.
items.acceptance: Provide a scalable test-plan template and example linking scope/risks/strategy/cases/environment/owners/schedule/entry-exit/suspension/resumption and evidence.

items.title: Demonstration, preventive, destruction and evaluation testing mindsets
items.gap: No explicit method for choosing these four mindsets or checking optimism bias across lifecycle artifacts.
items.acceptance: Use the source categories as optional review prompts and show how preventive/review/adversarial evidence complements happy paths.

items.title: Testbed setup, data, lifecycle and shared resource management
items.gap: No testbed inventory/provisioning/maintenance/sharing/capacity procedure covering OS/database/network/storage and remote environments.
items.acceptance: Provide an environment manifest/runbook with versions, fixtures, access, setup/cleanup, sharing limits, health checks and known fidelity gaps.

items.title: Automation strategy, tool selection and script maintenance
items.gap: No framework/tool-selection rubric for compatibility, reporting, cross-platform support, team skills, cost/support and maintenance ownership.
items.acceptance: Create optional decision rubric and plan linking automation goals, selected cases, compatible framework/tool, reporting, execution environments and upkeep cost/owner.

items.title: Test-strategy risks and contingency planning
items.gap: No test-strategy risk register for tool failure, unavailable testbed/model/resource or business/technology changes with contingency triggers.
items.acceptance: Add optional test-risk/trigger/mitigation/contingency/owner fields and demonstrate response to an unavailable test environment.

items.title: Test work breakdown, estimates, calendar and milestones
items.gap: No test activity estimates/calendar, milestone tracking or schedule-risk trigger method. Dependency order is not a schedule.
items.acceptance: Break down strategy/case/environment/execution/reporting work, estimate with assumptions, calendarize dependencies and identify milestone risk triggers.

items.title: Testing people, skills and infrastructure allocation
items.gap: Missing tester/developer/admin/SQA role capacity, infrastructure needs, sharing constraints and schedule feedback.
items.acceptance: Provide optional resource/skill/infrastructure inventory and adjust a test schedule to actual capacity and availability.

items.title: Test progress, defect severity and planning/control metrics
items.gap: No planned/created/executed coverage/status aggregation, defect severity/aging/escape report or schedule-control interpretation.
items.acceptance: Provide optional test progress aggregation with explicit denominators/statuses/severity, limitations and decisions; avoid developer ranking or simplistic issue/KLOC targets.

items.title: Requirements-linked security validation plan
items.gap: No integrated security plan binding each requirement/objective to method, component, owner, SDLC timing, tool/environment and execution evidence.
items.acceptance: Provide an optional security validation schema/template with these fields and traceability checks, plus a worked plan and blocked/skipped handling; never treat a schema pass as security certification.

items.title: Project lifecycle, leadership responsibilities and scope/time/cost tradeoffs
items.gap: Small-slice scope, dependencies, risks and owners are actionable. Lifecycle initiation/closure, budget/resource allocation, stakeholder communication and manager leadership/mentoring remain coordination concerns rather than a project-management procedure. Initiation, closing, organization, staffing and costing need an explicit procedure when the project requires them.
items.acceptance: Provide a proportionate project-plan procedure that records constraints, deliverables, resources/budget, stakeholder responsibilities, review/closure conditions and tradeoff decisions; demonstrate a multi-person example without forcing ceremony on a solo edit.

items.title: Agile release/iteration planning, story estimates and velocity
items.gap: INVEST, dependency/learning-value slicing and incremental delivery are guided. No worked release-versus-iteration planning procedure, story-point calibration, velocity/capacity calculation or handling unavailable customers/distributed teams. The source timeboxes and never-extend rule should be contextual, not universal.
items.acceptance: Use a backlog with historical completed work and availability to select a feasible increment; show revised scope under a deadline and state uncertainty/point limitations. A text workflow and worked example suffice.

items.title: Basic COCOMO effort, duration and staffing calculations
items.gap: No formulas, mode coefficients, validated input contract or worked calculation in actionable Sui guidance. PDF p.32 visually confirms E=a*KLOC^b, T=c*E^d and mean staffing E/T, with organic/semi-detached/embedded coefficient table. Intermediate/detailed models are named only in source.
items.acceptance: Add a clearly historical basic-COCOMO worked procedure or calculator with mode, KLOC, units, coefficients, E/T and sensitivity; reject invalid values; distinguish model estimate from calibrated project commitment. Do not advertise intermediate/detailed COCOMO merely from names.

items.title: Scheduling constraints, durations, milestones and resource feasibility
items.gap: Dependencies/readiness exist, but duration/calendar, resource/effort validation, explicit milestones and fixed-date versus effort-derived schedule treatment are not implemented. A topological ready list is not a schedule.
items.acceptance: Demonstrate a dependency schedule with durations, milestones and resource assumptions; identify an infeasible fixed deadline and revise scope or resources transparently. If automation is claimed, verify calculations against a hand-worked DAG.

items.title: RACI responsibility assignment
items.gap: RACI is named but not operationalized: no R/A/C/I definitions, one-accountable-person rule, matrix example or ambiguity check. Owner fields alone do not cover consultation/information responsibilities.
items.acceptance: Add an optional RACI text/table procedure for coordination: one A and explicit Rs, Cs, Is per activity; show how conflicting or missing accountability is resolved. No bespoke script required.

items.title: Project plan, monitoring/control and change communication
items.gap: Useful task/requirement/check state and source-drift controls exist. Full project plan coverage (staffing, budget, standards, communication, resource and quality plans) and periodic schedule/cost trend correction remain references.
items.acceptance: Produce a lean project plan and a review cycle linking observed progress, changed scope/risk/effort, decisions, owners and updated schedule. Keep state declarations separate from verified outcomes.

items.title: Gantt charts, critical path/slack and project-tool use
items.gap: Visual pp.51-52 and 54 show Microsoft Project/Gantt bars, milestones, resources, dependency lines and critical activities. No Gantt creation/update procedure, longest-duration-path or slack computation, nor Jira/MS Project integration.
items.acceptance: Given a duration-labelled DAG, compute earliest/latest times, slack and all critical paths and render/update a coherent Gantt chart. A documented use of a project-native tool is sufficient if actual tool capability is observed; distinguish Jira mention from implemented integration.

items.title: Team composition, cohesion, knowledge sharing and communication
items.gap: Teamwork is indexed and ownership is encouraged; there is no practical workflow for skills/capacity mix, team communication, knowledge-sharing and turnover continuity. Social-event examples are context, not mandatory practices.
items.acceptance: Offer a small-team coordination procedure with skill/owner/dependency visibility, handover and feedback cadence; demonstrate how it changes for team constraints. Do not claim to improve morale from a template.

items.title: Architecture documentation, notation and traceability
items.gap: ADR and optional diagrams are supported. Full architecture-document views (logical/process/deployment/use case), hierarchical decomposition, legend/edge semantics and diagram validation lack a practical checklist/example.
items.acceptance: Add a concise documentation procedure selecting views by decision/audience, declaring node/edge meaning and mapping quality constraints to evidence. Provide one readable checked example; avoid a mandatory heavyweight document.

items.title: UML component diagrams, interfaces, ports and dependencies
items.gap: A diagram is suggested, but no Sui procedure defines component notation, provided/required interfaces, ports, assembly connectors, dependency direction or subsystem examples. Visual pp.154/158/159 contain substantive interface/dependency models omitted by extraction.
items.acceptance: Add a concise component-model guide with component responsibilities, provided/required interfaces, correctly directed dependencies and notation legend, plus one internally consistent shopping/ATM or project example. Text/vector examples suffice; no special renderer is required.

items.title: Seven cohesion categories as design diagnostics
items.gap: Names and the high-cohesion goal exist; Sui lacks definitions/distinguishing examples for coincidental, logical, temporal, procedural, communicational, sequential and functional cohesion. A seven-name list is not a demonstrated diagnostic procedure.
items.acceptance: Add concise distinctions and examples, including input routines, initialization and read/print, then show a justified refactor using responsibility and change pressure rather than ranking labels alone.

items.title: Six coupling categories and interface diagnosis
items.gap: Concrete shared-state/control-flag cautions cover part of the material; no distinguishing examples or complete diagnostic procedure for all six kinds.
items.acceptance: Add contract-level examples of all six categories, demonstrate why a whole-structure parameter can bind consumers, and propose a compatible boundary reduction. Do not force every design to scalar-only interfaces.

items.title: Historical OO methods and structured analysis/DFD
items.gap: The source names Booch/Fusion and describes structured analysis/DFD to structure-chart design. Sui has no corresponding method procedure; the historical names alone are context, while useful data-flow modelling remains an available reference.
items.acceptance: If practical structured modelling is in scope, add a minimal levelled DFD procedure identifying processes, stores, external entities and balanced flows. Historical method trivia needs no runtime feature.

items.title: UML sequence models, alternatives and interactions
items.gap: Sui suggests sequence diagrams without participant/lifeline/message/return/activation/alt/loop guidance. Visual p.181 contains success/authorization-failure alternatives; p.182 includes loop/transfer interactions. Other UML types are merely listed on p.179.
items.acceptance: Add a short sequence-modelling guide/example with correct participant order, synchronous/asynchronous/return semantics and relevant alternatives/loops; check against a real use case. Do not count listed class/state diagrams as taught capabilities.

items.title: Clear API contracts and REST/OpenAPI/gRPC specifications
items.gap: Substantive interface design guidance exists. No contract-first OpenAPI or protobuf validation/generation procedure, worked schema, schema-implementation drift check or protocol selection example. Source snippets are illustrations, not bundled validated tool assets.
items.acceptance: Provide a small validated OpenAPI or protobuf example with inputs/outputs/errors and client/consumer compatibility tests, or documented project-native tooling. Treat protocol performance claims as workload-specific.

items.title: Function/library and IPC contracts
items.gap: Generic interface and lifetime reasoning covers part of the source. POSIX file I/O/shared-memory procedures, synchronization, permissions, message format and cleanup examples are interface examples; no checked native/IPC integration example.
items.acceptance: For a native/IPC task define ownership/lifetime, return/error contract, synchronization, permissions and cleanup; verify an actual caller/callee example. Do not copy the abbreviated source code as production-safe.

items.title: Synchronous/asynchronous API choice and completion semantics
items.gap: The distinction is named and related failure guidance exists, but no explicit blocking/completion/callback/cancellation/backpressure selection procedure or worked example. Source broad claims about runtime defaults need version-specific checking.
items.acceptance: Add a short choice guide with latency/workload/responsiveness constraints, completion/error/cancellation semantics and an example distinguishing concurrency from nonblocking I/O; test the relevant runtime boundary.

items.title: Error taxonomy, propagation and caller recovery
items.gap: Generic error and resource handling is substantive. No concrete structured error-code contract/registry, scoped namespaces, recovery documentation or cross-module error-version policy; C/Python examples remain source references.
items.acceptance: Add a language-appropriate result/exception/status example and optional shared error registry with stable codes, safe details, propagation, caller action and tests. Preserve existing project conventions rather than requiring one error strategy universally.

items.title: Structured logs, severity and request correlation
items.gap: Observability and privacy guidance exists; no explicit structured log schema/severity taxonomy/correlation-ID propagation procedure or tested cross-module example. Linking OpenTelemetry alone is a reference.
items.acceptance: Define minimal timestamp/module/error-code/request-ID fields, propagate an ID over a representative flow, test redaction and log a failure at the appropriate boundary without duplication or secrets.

items.title: Usability qualities, accessible design, error prevention and undo
items.gap: Accessibility/task observation and general safety/undo principles are guided. No LESEM-based interface review, clear-label/low-overload/recovery checklist, cognitive walkthrough or task-analysis procedure. Source UI photos and Hawaii/Therac history are examples, not automated usability evaluation.
items.acceptance: Provide a task-based checklist for learnability, efficiency, satisfaction, errors and memorability, plus keyboard/focus/accessibility and reversible/error-preventing controls; show concrete findings from an actual interface and retest improvements.

items.title: Real-user usability tests, task metrics and dogfooding
items.gap: Observing a prototype is guided, but no participant/task protocol, success/time/help/error measures, low-cost test cadence, dogfooding bias handling or synthesis/retest procedure. Visual p.227 is an illustrative saturation curve, not proof of a universal participant number.
items.acceptance: Create a concise user-study protocol with target participants, realistic tasks, consent/data handling where applicable, observable outcomes and decision thresholds; distinguish team dogfooding from representative-user evidence; record results honestly.

items.title: Usability study methods, A/B tests and prototypes
items.gap: Sui lacks a practical method-selection guide for lab/field/shadowing/interviews/surveys and mockup/paper/Wizard-of-Oz prototypes, or a randomized A/B design with exposure/outcome/sample/uncertainty. Generic comparisons do not implement an experiment.
items.acceptance: Add guidance choosing method by question, participant access, reactivity/cost and qualitative versus causal evidence; give a bounded prototype test and an A/B example with randomization, unit of analysis, metric and uncertainty. No generic statistics engine is required.

items.title: Cost of quality: prevention/appraisal/internal/external failures
items.gap: No operational COQ/COGQ/COPQ procedure, cost taxonomy, unit/window or worked business tradeoff. General cost awareness and debt guidance do not calculate cost of quality.
items.acceptance: Add a small worked cost ledger splitting prevention/appraisal and internal/external failure, stating time window/currency/assumptions and avoiding double counting; connect an improvement decision to uncertainty. A table/text calculation is sufficient.

items.title: SQA plan, process audits, deviations and responsibility
items.gap: Component review/test/release controls are guided and some helpers execute checks. No integrated SQA plan addressing responsibility, document/design/development control, training, audit cadence, defect/deviation tracking and noncompliance reporting. A passing validator is not organizational SQA.
items.acceptance: Provide a proportionate SQA-plan/checklist with owners, lifecycle controls, evidence, deviation handling and review cadence; demonstrate an audit finding and follow-up on a concrete project without manufacturing compliance.

items.title: Test-driven development red/green/refactor loop
items.gap: Regression-first suggestions overlap with TDD, but there is no explicit opt-in red/green/refactor procedure: write a small behavioral test, observe intended red, minimum change to green, refactor and rerun. No forward TDD task demonstration is present. A source TDD mention is not implementation.
items.acceptance: Add a practical opt-in TDD workflow and one demonstration recording intended failure before code, minimal passing implementation and behavior-preserving refactor with passing tests. State that TDD does not guarantee all paths or requirements are covered.

items.title: Collection/cleaning/labels/features, train/eval splits, model deployment/monitoring/retraining and MLOps
items.gap: No concrete training-serving/retraining workflow, model/data compatibility gate, or worked feedback-loop example; eval_report.py summarizes supplied judgments rather than trains, serves or monitors models.
items.acceptance: Add a concise ML pipeline playbook linking data/feature/model versions, validation, training-serving skew, release/rollback, drift and retraining triggers. A reproducible fixture is needed only if claiming executable MLOps support.

items.title: Sprint burndown, velocity, throughput and cycle time
items.gap: No concrete calculation/interpretation guidance for work remaining, scope changes, velocity comparability, throughput or cycle-time distributions.
items.acceptance: Add a short team-level worked example with denominators, window and scope-change caveat; do not claim story points measure individual productivity or business value. A dashboard adapter is optional.

items.title: Peer review, unit/test-first, pair programming, stepping, debugging and inspections
items.gap: Pair-programming driver/navigator practice, explicit test-first cycle and formal inspection roles need a selectable construction-quality workflow.
items.acceptance: Add proportionate decision guidance for pairing, test-first, stepping and inspection. Demonstrate selected method in conversation; automation is unnecessary for pairing or review meetings.

items.title: Reviewable PR titles/descriptions with context, rationale, links and visual evidence
items.gap: No explicit Sui PR-description workflow/template connecting trigger/before-after behavior, rationale, relevant issues/specs, validation and UI screenshots. General final-report guidance only partially covers this artifact.
items.acceptance: Add concise PR-description guidance or a conditional template with those fields, honoring repository templates and scope; do not require every field for a tiny patch.

items.title: Local source/binaries, remote server and browser code; white/gray/black-box limits
items.gap: No explicit local-binary/remote-opaque/browser capability decision table or setup examples; IDE configuration, remote attach and browser probes are reference-only.
items.acceptance: Add a concise environment matrix describing available evidence/edit boundaries and appropriate probes. Implement adapters only for selected environments; never invent source access or execute fetched code by default.

items.title: Static-analysis capabilities, undecidability, conservative approximations, false positives/negatives
items.gap: No developed taxonomy, conservative-analysis/false-positive triage workflow, diff-based baseline policy or n2s worked exercise; most details remain extracted reference.
items.acceptance: Add concise selection/triage guidance for lint, pattern, annotation and data-flow analyses with approximation/performance tradeoffs, suppression ownership and a small example. No general static analyzer must be built.

items.title: Type annotations/nullability, units, dependent annotations and reflection/generated-code limits
items.gap: No actionable nullable/non-null/units example, library annotation/stub policy or generated-code false-positive handling in the implementation guidance.
items.acceptance: Add one project-adapted nullness/units contract example and guidance for library stubs/generated code; tool-specific adapters are evaluated separately.

items.title: SpotBugs support
items.gap: No SpotBugs adapter, version/config recipe, output parser/normalization, suppression baseline or clean/defective fixture tests. Generic command execution is not tool integration.
items.acceptance: If SpotBugs support is selected or advertised, add version-aware setup/config, bounded invocation, finding/exit semantics and clean/failing/malformed-output fixtures; otherwise label it external/historical/reference instead of implemented.

items.title: Dominos accessibility and airline family-seating incentives
items.gap: Accessibility has usable guidance; manipulative design and family-seating incentive analysis is only background context. No explicit dark-pattern or conflicting-incentive decision example.
items.acceptance: Add a brief harmful-incentive/design choice example covering vulnerable users, transparency and alternatives; apply project-appropriate accessibility checks without pretending an old legal case establishes present jurisdictional duties.

items.title: Ethics discourse, ACM commitments and limits of codes
items.gap: No explicit decision aid covering well-being/harm/honesty/fairness/non-discrimination/property/credit/privacy/confidentiality or how to act when a code alone changes little.
items.acceptance: Add a concise stakeholder/consequence/options/accountability review mapped to the named ACM commitments, with uncertainty and actionable escalation. Do not claim a checkbox or code citation guarantees ethical outcomes.

items.title: LLM training provenance, output ownership and sensitive inputs
items.gap: No explicit questions/record for model training provenance and generated-output rights in the intended deployment. Current law/provider terms cannot be inferred from a general summary.
items.acceptance: Add a bounded provenance/terms/input-confidentiality checklist and one provider-independent example, with verified current primary terms for actual decisions and unknown rights explicitly marked; avoid blanket ownership or legality conclusions.

items.title: Five flourishing domains, three ethical questions and predictive-attendance exercise
items.gap: No usable five-domain/three-question review or worked attendance/social-media case. The review covers happiness/life satisfaction, mental/physical health, meaning/purpose, character/virtue and close relationships.
items.acceptance: Add the three review questions (respect humanity; amplify positive/negative behavior; quality impact on others) and one predictive-attendance example assessing the five domains, consent/privacy/fairness, alternatives and residual uncertainty. No executable ethical score is required.
